canary.method: openpyxl writes formulas with NO cached <v> value; `soffice --headless --convert-to xlsx` must evaluate every formula from scratch to produce any output value at all. The volatile =NOW() canary changing between two runs a few seconds apart, plus the deterministic arithmetic canary matching exactly, together prove genuine recalculation.

CEILING.MATH_basic_significance.description: Rounds 24.3 up to the nearest multiple of 5. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ceiling-math-function-80f95d2f-b499-4eee-9f16-f795a8e306c8 (worked example table)

CEILING.MATH_default_significance_1.description: Significance and mode both omitted -> defaults to nearest integer (significance 1). Source: Microsoft CEILING.MATH docs.

CEILING.MATH_negative_default_mode_towar.description: Negative number, mode omitted -> unlike the modeless legacy CEILING function, CEILING.MATH's default for negative numbers rounds TOWARD zero.
CEILING.MATH_negative_default_mode_towar.notes: Microsoft worked example: CEILING.MATH(-8.1,2) = -8 ('rounds -8.1 up (toward 0) to the nearest multiple of 2'). This is the modern, explicit-mode successor to legacy CEILING and was designed to match LibreOffice/ODF's CEILING(...,...,Mode) semantics for the default case.

CEILING.MATH_negative_mode_nonzero_away_.description: Negative number with a nonzero mode argument -> rounds away from zero instead of the toward-zero default.
CEILING.MATH_negative_mode_nonzero_away_.notes: Microsoft worked example: CEILING.MATH(-5.5,2,-1) = -6 ('rounds -5.5 down (away from 0) ... with a mode of -1'). Mode only affects negative numbers; any nonzero mode reverses the default direction.

CEILING_PRECISE_basic.description: Rounds up to the nearest multiple of 3

CEILING_PRECISE_already_multiple.description: A value already on a multiple is returned unchanged

CEILING_PRECISE_negative_rounds_up.description: Unlike CEILING, PRECISE always rounds toward positive infinity regardless of the significance sign, so -7 rounds up to -6

CEILING_basic.description: Basic case, rounds 2.5 up to the nearest multiple of 1. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ceiling-function-0a5cd7c8-0720-4f0a-bd2c-c943e510899f (worked example table)

CEILING_fractional_significance.description: Rounds 0.234 up to the nearest multiple of 0.01. Source: Microsoft CEILING docs worked example table.

CEILING_both_negative_away_from_zero.description: Number and significance both negative -> rounds away from zero (more negative), per Microsoft's documented rule and worked example.
CEILING_both_negative_away_from_zero.notes: Microsoft: 'If number is negative, and significance is negative, the value is rounded down, away from zero.' Worked example CEILING(-2.5,-2)=-4 at https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ceiling-function-0a5cd7c8-0720-4f0a-bd2c-c943e510899f

CEILING_negative_number_positive_signifi.description: Number negative, significance positive -> rounds up toward zero (less negative), per Microsoft's documented rule and worked example.
CEILING_negative_number_positive_signifi.notes: Microsoft: 'If number is negative, and significance is positive, the value is rounded up towards zero.' Worked example CEILING(-2.5,2)=-2 at the same doc page.

CEILING_libreoffice_default_mode_diverge.description: GOLD QUIRK CANDIDATE: identical 2-argument call (Mode omitted) with number and significance both negative. Per Microsoft's documented CEILING rule this must round AWAY from zero.
CEILING_libreoffice_default_mode_diverge.notes: Microsoft (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ceiling-function-0a5cd7c8-0720-4f0a-bd2c-c943e510899f): both-negative case rounds away from zero, so CEILING(-45.67,-2) -> -46 (ratio -45.67/-2=22.835, ceiling(22.835)=23, 23*-2=-46). LibreOffice's own CEILING docs (https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/scalc/01/func_ceiling.html) define a 3rd optional Mode argument that ONLY applies when both Number and Significance are negative, and state: 'if Mode is equal to zero or not given, negative numbers are rounded up (towards zero)' -- with LO's own worked example CEILING(-45.67;-2;0) = -44. That means the identical 2-arg formula (Mode omitted) is documented to resolve to -44 under LibreOffice's own default, vs -46 under Microsoft's documented default -- a genuine cross-engine default-behavior divergence for the exact same formula text, not just a wording difference. If LO's executed result is -44, matched_expected:false here is the intended, correct signal of that divergence -- do not 'fix' this expectation to match LO.

CEILING_nonnumeric_error.description: Nonnumeric first argument -> #VALUE!, per Microsoft docs: 'If either argument is nonnumeric, CEILING returns the #VALUE! error value.'

CHAR_out_of_range_zero.description: 0 is outside CHAR's documented valid range of 1-255 -> #VALUE!
CHAR_out_of_range_zero.notes: Microsoft docs: CHAR takes "A number between 1 and 255 specifying which character you want." Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/char-function-bbd249c8-b36e-4a91-8017-1c133f9b837a; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#VALUE!', got '_x0000_'

CHAR_out_of_range_256.description: 256 is above CHAR's documented valid range of 1-255 -> #VALUE!
CHAR_out_of_range_256.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/char-function-bbd249c8-b36e-4a91-8017-1c133f9b837a - valid range is 1-255; values outside it are invalid

CHOOSE_basic_second_value.description: index_num=2 selects the second value in the list

CHOOSE_out_of_range_error.description: index_num beyond the number of supplied values -> #VALUE!
CHOOSE_out_of_range_error.notes: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/choose-function-fc5c184f-cb62-4ec7-a46e-38653b98f5bc -- 'If index_num is less than 1 or greater than the number of the last value in the list, CHOOSE returns the #VALUE! error value.'

CHOOSE_fractional_index_truncated.description: Non-integer index_num is truncated toward the lowest integer before use, not rounded
CHOOSE_fractional_index_truncated.notes: Same doc as above: 'If index_num is a fraction, it is truncated to the lowest integer before being used.' 2.9 truncates to 2, not rounded to 3

CHOOSE_selects_a_range_then_summed.description: CHOOSE can select an entire range as its 'value', which is then fed to SUM
CHOOSE_selects_a_range_then_summed.notes: index_num=2 selects the B1:B3 range; SUM of 10+20+30=60

CHOOSECOLS_pick_3_1.description: Return columns 3 and 1 of a row, in that order
CHOOSECOLS_pick_3_1.notes: MISMATCH vs expected: value mismatch: expected 3, got '#NAME?'

CHOOSEROWS_pick_4_2.description: Return rows 4 and 2 of a column, in that order
CHOOSEROWS_pick_4_2.notes: MISMATCH vs expected: value mismatch: expected 40, got '#NAME?'

CLEAN_removes_control_char.description: CHAR(7) (BEL, a non-printable 7-bit ASCII control character) is stripped out

CLEAN_removes_tab_leaves_text.description: CLEAN removes CHAR(9) (tab) because it's one of the first 32 non-printable ASCII codes -- contrast with TRIM, which leaves tabs completely untouched since TRIM only targets the space character (32), not control characters
CLEAN_removes_tab_leaves_text.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/clean-function-26f3d7c5-475f-4a9c-90e5-4b8ba987ba41 - CLEAN "removes nonprintable characters from ASCII codes 0 through 31"; its own documented example uses CHAR(9)&"Monthly report"&CHAR(10) -> "Monthly report"

CLEAN_leaves_spaces_alone.description: Regular space characters (code 32) are left alone by CLEAN -- only non-printable control characters (codes 0-31) are removed

CLEAN_no_op_on_clean_text.description: Text with no non-printable characters passes through unchanged

CODE_first_character_only.description: CODE only looks at the first character of a multi-character string
CODE_first_character_only.notes: Microsoft docs: CODE "Returns a numeric code for the first character in a text string." Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/code-function-c32b692b-2ed0-4a04-bdd9-75640144b928

CODE_char_roundtrip.description: CODE and CHAR are exact inverses of each other for values 1-255

COLUMN_no_arg_uses_formula_cell.description: No argument: COLUMN() returns the column of the cell containing the formula itself. This case's formula lands in F1 by default, and F is the 6th column
COLUMN_no_arg_uses_formula_cell.notes: F is column 6; COLUMN() with no anchor argument returns the formula's own column

COLUMN_explicit_cell_ref.description: Explicit single-cell reference argument overrides the formula's own location

COLUMN_range_returns_first_column.description: In non-array (scalar) context, COLUMN() of a multi-column range returns the column number of the FIRST column of the reference

COLUMN_far_column.description: Sanity check with a larger column number (Z is the 26th column)

COLUMNS_basic_row_range.description: Width (column count) of a single-row range; does not depend on cell contents

COLUMNS_single_cell.description: A single cell reference has exactly 1 column

COLUMNS_2d_range.description: Column count of a 2-D range only counts columns, ignoring the 4 rows

COMBINA_basic.description: Combinations WITH repetition of 3 from 4 items: C(4+3-1,3) = C(6,3) = 20

COMBINA_choose_zero.description: Choosing zero items always gives exactly one combination

CONCAT_range.description: CONCAT flattens a range directly (unlike CONCATENATE, which cannot take a range)

CONCAT_mixed_types.description: Numbers are coerced to text without an explicit TEXT() call

CONCATENATE_cell_refs.description: Join cells with a space separator

CONVERT_celsius_to_fahrenheit.description: Temperature conversion applies the correct offset: 100 C = 212 F

CORREL_perfect_linear.description: y=2x exactly, so the correlation coefficient must be exactly 1

COUNT_mixed_types_range.description: COUNT only counts numeric cells in a range; text, blanks, and booleans (when referenced via a range) are all excluded
COUNT_mixed_types_range.notes: A3 and A6 are blank, A2 is text, A4 is a boolean cell; only A1=10 and A5=20 are counted; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 2, got 3

COUNT_boolean_in_range_excluded.description: A boolean value referenced through a cell range is NOT counted by COUNT
COUNT_boolean_in_range_excluded.notes: Per Microsoft's COUNT documentation, booleans in a referenced range are excluded from COUNT, unlike booleans typed directly as literal arguments; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 0, got 1

COUNT_boolean_literal_argument_counted.description: Contrast with COUNT_boolean_in_range_excluded: a logical value typed directly into the argument list IS counted
COUNT_boolean_literal_argument_counted.notes: Microsoft's COUNT docs: "Logical values and text representations of numbers that you type directly into the list of arguments are counted" - this differs from the same boolean sitting in a cell reference

COUNT_all_blank_range.description: A range with no values at all counts as 0

COUNTA_mixed_types_range.description: COUNTA counts every non-blank cell regardless of type: numbers, text, and booleans all count, unlike COUNT which only counts numbers (same setup as COUNT_mixed_types_range)
COUNTA_mixed_types_range.notes: A1, A2, A4, A5 are all non-blank (A3, A6 are genuinely blank and excluded)

COUNTA_empty_string_formula_counts.description: A cell holding a formula that returns "" is still counted by COUNTA, because it contains content (a formula), even though it displays as empty. Confirmed via Microsoft's COUNTA docs (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/counta-function-7dc98875-d5c1-46f1-9a82-53f3219e2509): "if the range contains a formula that returns an empty string, the COUNTA function counts that value."
COUNTA_empty_string_formula_counts.notes: Both A1 (formula returning "") and A2 (5) are counted; this same A1 cell is ALSO counted as blank by COUNTBLANK - see COUNTBLANK_empty_string_formula_counted_as_blank

COUNTA_all_blank_range.description: A range with no content at all counts as 0

COUNTBLANK_basic.description: Counts genuinely empty cells in a range
COUNTBLANK_basic.notes: A2 and A4 are the blank cells

COUNTBLANK_mixed_types_range.description: Same mixed range as COUNT/COUNTA: only the genuinely empty cells count, not the text/number/boolean cells

COUNTBLANK_empty_string_formula_counted_.description: Documented cross-engine-relevant edge case: a cell containing a formula that returns "" is counted as blank by COUNTBLANK, same as a truly empty cell - even though that identical cell would be counted as non-blank by COUNTA (see COUNTA_empty_string_formula_counts). Confirmed via Microsoft's COUNTBLANK docs (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/countblank-function-6a92d772-675c-4bee-b346-24af6bd3ac22): "Cells with formulas that return "" (empty text) are also counted."
COUNTBLANK_empty_string_formula_counted_.notes: A1 is truly blank (not set at all) and A2's formula result of "" is ALSO counted as blank -> 2 total; only A3=5 is excluded

COUNTBLANK_zero_not_blank.description: A cell containing the number 0 is NOT counted as blank

COUNTIF_case_insensitive_text_match.description: Text comparisons in COUNTIF are case-insensitive
COUNTIF_case_insensitive_text_match.notes: Both 'apple' and 'Apple' match the literal 'APPLE' criteria regardless of case

COUNTIF_criteria_from_cell_concat.description: Dynamic criteria built by concatenating an operator with a cell reference

COUNTIFS_multi_range.notes: Rows 2,3 satisfy A>10 AND B<5 (rows 4,5 fail B<5); rows matching: (20,2),(30,3)

COVAR_positive.description: Population covariance of two perfectly co-varying columns (B = 2A)

COVAR_constant_column.description: When one variable never changes there is no covariance

COVARIANCE_P_positive.description: Population covariance of two perfectly co-varying columns (B = 2A); the modern equivalent of COVAR

COVARIANCE_P_constant_column.description: When one variable never changes there is no covariance

COVARIANCE_S_positive.description: Sample covariance (divides by n-1) of two perfectly co-varying columns (B = 2A)

COVARIANCE_S_constant_column.description: When one variable never changes there is no covariance

CUMIPMT_first_period.description: Cumulative interest over just period 1 (negative by cash-flow convention) = -1500

CUMPRINC_first_period.description: Cumulative principal over period 1 (negative by convention) = -298.65

DATE_month_rollover_above_12.description: Documented rollover: month=13 adds 13 months worth of offset from January, landing in January of the FOLLOWING year rather than raising an error. Verified via https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/date-function-e36c0c8c-4104-49da-ab83-82328b832349 ("If month is greater than 12 ... DATE(2008,14,2) returns ... February 2, 2009")
DATE_month_rollover_above_12.notes: month 13 = 12 months past January 2024 -> January 2025; 2025-01-01 = serial 45658 (2024 is a leap year, 366 days after 45292)

DATE_month_rollback_below_1.description: Documented rollback: month<=0 subtracts months backward across a year boundary. Verified via the same DATE documentation ("If month is less than 1 ... DATE(2008,-3,2) returns ... September 2, 2007")

DATEDIF_md_known_quirk.description: "MD" (days ignoring months and years) is documented by Microsoft as unreliable/buggy for some date combos
DATEDIF_md_known_quirk.notes: Textbook-naive expectation might be ~1, but MD has a well-known Microsoft-acknowledged bug around month-end dates; recording the ACTUAL engine output is the point of this test

DATEDIF_end_before_start.description: End date before start date -> #NUM! per Microsoft's documented DATEDIF behavior
DATEDIF_end_before_start.notes: Microsoft docs state end<start raises #NUM!; record engines' ACTUAL error code here since this is a known point of cross-engine divergence; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#NUM!', got '#VALUE!'

DATEVALUE_iso.description: Parse an ISO date string to its serial number

DAVERAGE_matching_criteria.description: Averages the Sales column for rows matching the criteria (Region = East)

DAVERAGE_numeric_criteria.description: Averages Sales for rows where Sales is greater than 75

DAY_of_date.description: DAY applied to a constructed date

DAY_of_raw_serial_epoch.description: DAY applied directly to the raw serial number 1 (Jan 1, 1900)
DAY_of_raw_serial_epoch.notes: Serial 1 is Jan 1, 1900 in the 1900 date system; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 1, got 31

DAY_ignores_time_fraction.description: A serial with a fractional (time-of-day) component still resolves to the correct calendar day
DAY_ignores_time_fraction.notes: 45366 = 2024-03-15; the .75 fractional day is ignored by DAY

DAYS_basic_end_first_argument_order.description: DAYS takes END_DATE FIRST, then start_date -- the opposite argument order from DAYS360/YEARFRAC. Verified via https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/days-function-57740535-d549-4395-8728-0f07bff0b9df ("DAYS(end_date, start_date)")

DAYS_reversed_arguments_flip_sign.description: Swapping which date is passed first (now the earlier date is 'end_date') flips the sign -- reinforcing that argument order is significant and not auto-corrected
DAYS_reversed_arguments_flip_sign.notes: Same two dates as DAYS_basic_end_first_argument_order but with roles swapped -> -14

DAYS_doc_example_text_dates.description: Microsoft's own documented example, using text dates parsed as if by DATEVALUE
DAYS_doc_example_text_dates.notes: Exact example from the DAYS function documentation

DAYS_doc_example_full_year.description: A second literal example from the same Microsoft documentation page

DAYS360_doc_example_basic.description: Microsoft's own documented example, default (US/NASD) method. Verified via https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/days360-function-b9a509fd-49ef-407e-94df-0cbda5718c2a

DAYS360_doc_example_full_year.description: A second literal example from the same documentation page, showing the 30-day-month/360-day-year convention

DAYS360_us_method_month_end_shift.description: US (NASD) method month-end rule: end_date is the last day of its month (Jan 31) and start_date (Jan 1) is before the 30th, so end_date shifts to the 1st of the NEXT month (Feb 1) before the 30/360 day count. Verified via the DAYS360 documentation's description of the US method's end-of-month handling

DAYS360_european_method_month_end_no_shi.description: Same date pair as DAYS360_us_method_month_end_shift but method=TRUE (European method): the European rule simply clamps day-31 dates to day 30, with none of the US method's 'shift end_date to next month' logic, giving a genuinely DIFFERENT result (29, not 30) for the identical inputs -- the documented US-vs-European divergence
DAYS360_european_method_month_end_no_shi.notes: Effective dates become Jan 1 -> Jan 30 (31 clamped to 30, no next-month shift) -> (1-1)*30 + (30-1) = 29

DB_first_year.description: Fixed-declining year 1: rate = 1-(salvage/cost)^(1/life) rounded to 3 places = 0.369, so 3690

DCOUNT_matching_criteria.description: Counts the numeric Sales entries for rows matching the criteria (Region = East)

DCOUNT_all_matching.description: With a criteria that matches every row, counts all numeric Sales entries

DEC2OCT_padded.description: The optional places argument pads the result to a fixed width with leading zeros

DECIMAL_basic.description: Parse hexadecimal text back to a number

DEGREES_negative.description: Negative radians convert to negative degrees (a quarter turn backward)

DEVSQ_basic.description: Sum of squared deviations from the mean (4): 4 + 0 + 4 = 8

DEVSQ_from_range.description: Sum of squared deviations of 1..5 from their mean of 3

DSUM_numeric_condition.description: Criteria can be a comparison expression, e.g. Sales greater than 75

EDATE_leap_year_clamp.notes: 2024 is a leap year; Feb has no 31st so EDATE clamps to Feb 29 = serial 45351

EDATE_negative_months.description: Negative months argument goes backward (2024-01-15 = serial 45306)

EDATE_fractional_months_truncated.description: Non-integer months argument is truncated toward zero, not rounded (2024-02-01 = serial 45323)

EOMONTH_crosses_year_boundary.description: Positive offset that also crosses a year boundary

ERROR.TYPE_ref.description: Offsetting above row 1 produces a genuine #REF! error -> code 4

FILTER_inline_array_literal.description: Filtering an inline array literal by an inline boolean/number mask

FIND_case_sensitive_no_match.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/office/find-function-06213f91-b5be-4544-8b0b-2fd5a775436f and https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/how-to-correct-a-value-error-in-find-findb-and-search-searchb-functions-0d1299aa-6234-4253-bc5e-50881b575fc6 - FIND is case-sensitive and does not support wildcard characters

FIND_not_found.description: find_text not present anywhere in within_text -> #VALUE!

FIND_start_num_skips_earlier_match.description: start_num=3 begins the search at position 3, skipping the earlier match of 'p' at position 2

FLOOR.MATH_basic_significance.description: Rounds 24.3 down to the nearest multiple of 5. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/floor-math-function-c302b599-fbdb-4177-ba19-2c2b1249a2f5 (worked example table)

FLOOR.MATH_default_significance_1.description: Significance and mode both omitted -> defaults to nearest integer (significance 1). Source: Microsoft FLOOR.MATH docs.

FLOOR.MATH_negative_default_mode_away_fr.description: Negative number, mode omitted -> FLOOR.MATH's default for negative numbers rounds AWAY from zero (opposite default direction from CEILING.MATH's toward-zero default).
FLOOR.MATH_negative_default_mode_away_fr.notes: Microsoft worked example: FLOOR.MATH(-8.1,2) = -10 ('rounds -8.1 down (away from 0) to the nearest integer that is a multiple of 2'). Note this default is the mirror image of CEILING.MATH's default (toward zero) for the same-shaped call.

FLOOR.MATH_negative_mode_nonzero_toward_.description: Negative number with a nonzero mode argument -> reverses the default to round toward zero instead of away from zero.
FLOOR.MATH_negative_mode_nonzero_toward_.notes: Microsoft worked example: FLOOR.MATH(-5.5,2,-1) = -4 ('rounds -5.5 toward 0 ... using a non-zero Mode, which reverses rounding direction').

FLOOR_basic.description: Basic case, rounds 3.7 down to the nearest multiple of 2. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/floor-function-14bb497c-24f2-4e04-b327-b0b4de5a8886 (worked example table)

FLOOR_fractional_significance.description: Rounds 0.234 down to the nearest multiple of 0.01. Source: Microsoft FLOOR docs worked example table.

FLOOR_both_negative_toward_zero.description: Number and significance both negative -> Microsoft's own worked example rounds this TOWARD zero (-2), which is the opposite direction CEILING takes for the same-signed case.
FLOOR_both_negative_toward_zero.notes: Microsoft's worked example table gives FLOOR(-2.5,-2) = -2 exactly (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/floor-function-14bb497c-24f2-4e04-b327-b0b4de5a8886). Note this is the OPPOSITE rounding direction of CEILING(-2.5,-2)=-4 for the identical arguments -- FLOOR and CEILING deliberately diverge on both-negative inputs, not a bug.

FLOOR_mismatched_sign_error.description: Number positive, significance negative (opposite signs) -> #NUM!, explicitly documented by Microsoft: 'If Number is positive and Significance is negative, FLOOR returns the #NUM! error value.'

FLOOR_libreoffice_default_mode_divergenc.description: GOLD QUIRK CANDIDATE: mirror image of the CEILING default-Mode divergence. Both Number and significance negative, Mode omitted.
FLOOR_libreoffice_default_mode_divergenc.notes: Derived from Microsoft's own worked FLOOR(-2.5,-2)=-2 example (both-negative case rounds TOWARD zero): ratio -45.67/-2=22.835, truncating toward zero gives 22, 22*-2=-44. LibreOffice's own FLOOR docs (https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/scalc/01/func_floor.html) define an optional 3rd Mode argument that only applies when both Number and Significance are negative, stating 'Mode = 0 or omitted: negative numbers are rounded down (away from zero)' with LO's own worked example FLOOR(-45.67;-2;0) = -46. So the identical 2-arg formula (Mode omitted) is documented to resolve to -46 under LibreOffice's default vs -44 under Microsoft's documented behavior -- a genuine divergence, and the exact mirror image of the CEILING case above (there Excel defaults away-from-zero and LO defaults toward-zero; here Excel defaults toward-zero and LO defaults away-from-zero). If LO's executed result is -46, matched_expected:false is the correct, intended signal -- do not 'fix' this expectation to match LO.

FLOOR_nonnumeric_error.description: Nonnumeric first argument -> #VALUE!, per Microsoft docs: 'If either argument is nonnumeric, FLOOR returns the #VALUE! error value.'

FORECAST_ETS_exists.description: Existence probe: exponential-smoothing forecast of the next point of a rising series. The AAA algorithm's exact output depends on implementation internals, so we only assert the engine recognizes the function and returns a numeric value (not #NAME?)
FORECAST_ETS_exists.notes: Non-deterministic across implementations by design (smoothing-parameter optimization differs); the key datum is whether the engine has FORECAST.ETS at all. Excel returns ~70 for this series.

FORECAST_LINEAR_two_point_interpolation.description: Modern renamed FORECAST (Excel 2016+): exact line through (2,10),(3,20) evaluated at 2.5 = 15

FORECAST_two_point_interpolation.description: Linear fit through (2,10) and (3,20): the line is exact, so x=2.5 must give exactly 15

FORECAST_extrapolation.description: Points (1,10),(2,20),(3,30) lie exactly on y=10x; extrapolating to x=5 gives 50

FORMULATEXT_basic_arithmetic.description: A cell holding a plain arithmetic formula -> FORMULATEXT returns the exact formula text as typed

FORMULATEXT_preserves_exact_text.description: Formula text with nested string literals is returned verbatim, including quotes

FORMULATEXT_non_formula_cell.description: A cell containing a plain (non-formula) value -> #N/A, per docs: 'The cell used as the Reference argument does not contain a formula.' Confirmed via https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/formulatext-function-0a786771-54fd-4ae2-96ee-09cda35439c8

FORMULATEXT_blank_cell.description: A blank cell has no formula either -> #N/A

FREQUENCY_three_bins.description: Data 1..5 with bin edges 2 and 4: counts are (<=2)=2, (3..4)=2, (>4)=1, spilled vertically

FV_monthly_savings.description: Future value of $100/month for 10 years at 5% annual, compounded monthly

GROUPBY_exists_sum.description: Existence probe: group a,b,a,b over 1,2,3,4 with SUM. In Excel 365 this spills grouped rows (a=4, b=6) plus a grand-total row by default; the exact spill layout depends on optional field_headers/total_depth arguments, so we only assert the engine recognizes the function (not #NAME?)
GROUPBY_exists_sum.notes: Probe only: layout of the spilled result (headers/totals) varies with optional args; the key datum is whether the engine has GROUPBY at all

GROWTH_exact_exponential.description: y=2^x data extrapolated to x=4 must give 16 (exact exponential fit)

HARMEAN_basic.description: Harmonic mean = n divided by the sum of reciprocals; 3/(1/2+1/3+1/6) = 3

HARMEAN_all_equal.description: The harmonic mean of identical values is that value

HARMEAN_from_range.description: Harmonic mean of two values read from cells; 2/(1/1+1/3) = 1.5

HEX2BIN_padded.description: The optional places argument pads the binary result to a fixed width

HEX2DEC_basic.description: Converts a hexadecimal text value to its decimal number

HEX2DEC_ten.description: The hex digit A is 10 in decimal

HEX2DEC_roundtrip.description: HEX2DEC reverses DEC2HEX, recovering the original number

HLOOKUP_exact_match.description: Exact match (range_lookup=FALSE) on a horizontal lookup table

HLOOKUP_approximate_match.description: Approximate match (TRUE) requires the first row sorted ascending; returns the largest header <= lookup_value
HLOOKUP_approximate_match.notes: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/hlookup-function-a3034eec-b719-4ba3-bb65-e1ad662ed95f -- approximate match finds the next largest value that is <= lookup_value; 6 falls between 5 and 7, so it matches 5 -> 50

HLOOKUP_not_found_exact_na.description: Exact match with no match found -> #N/A

HLOOKUP_row_index_out_of_range.description: row_index_num greater than the number of rows in table_array -> #REF!

HOUR_of_fractional_day_noon.description: HOUR applied to a bare fractional-day serial (no date part) -- 0.5 of a day is exactly noon

HOUR_of_time_value.description: HOUR applied to a TIME()-constructed value

HSTACK_two_columns.description: Horizontally join two 2-row columns into a 2x2 array
HSTACK_two_columns.notes: MISMATCH vs expected: value mismatch: expected 1, got '#NAME?'

HYPERLINK_with_friendly_name.description: Formula result (display text) is the friendly_name when supplied

HYPERLINK_without_friendly_name.description: With no friendly_name argument, the displayed result falls back to link_location itself

HYPERLINK_friendly_name_numeric.description: friendly_name may be a number; the formula result is that numeric value

HYPERLINK_friendly_name_from_cell.description: friendly_name supplied via a cell reference

IFERROR_no_error_passthrough.description: No error: original value passes through unchanged

IFERROR_nested_vlookup.description: Catches #N/A bubbling up from a failed VLOOKUP

IFERROR_indirect_missing_sheet.description: INDIRECT pointed at a sheet that does not exist in the workbook raises #REF!; IFERROR is documented as trapping ANY error value, so the fallback text should be returned
IFERROR_indirect_missing_sheet.notes: Microsoft documents IFERROR as returning value_if_error for any of #N/A, #VALUE!, #REF!, #DIV/0!, #NUM!, #NAME? and #NULL! -- #REF! is explicitly in that list, so the source of the #REF! (a missing sheet name inside INDIRECT) should not matter. Excel function reference: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/excel-functions-alphabetical-b3944572-255d-4efb-bb96-c6d90033e188; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 'missing', got '#REF!'

IFERROR_indirect_bad_text.description: Contrast case: the same IFERROR wrapper around an INDIRECT whose ref_text is simply not a valid reference (see INDIRECT_malformed_ref_error), which also raises #REF!
IFERROR_indirect_bad_text.notes: Same documented rule as IFERROR_indirect_missing_sheet: IFERROR traps #REF! whatever produced it. Excel function reference: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/excel-functions-alphabetical-b3944572-255d-4efb-bb96-c6d90033e188

IFNA_catches_na.description: #N/A from a failed MATCH is caught

IFNA_does_not_catch_other_errors.description: IFNA only catches #N/A; #DIV/0! must pass through unchanged
IFNA_does_not_catch_other_errors.notes: Common compat pitfall: IFNA is NOT a general error trap like IFERROR

IFNA_no_error_passthrough.description: No error: original value passes through

IFNA_indirect_missing_sheet.description: IFNA only traps #N/A, so the #REF! from an INDIRECT naming a missing sheet must pass straight through
IFNA_indirect_missing_sheet.notes: Documented scope difference, not a quirk: IFNA returns value_if_na for #N/A only, while IFERROR traps every error value. Excel function reference: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/excel-functions-alphabetical-b3944572-255d-4efb-bb96-c6d90033e188

IFS_basic.description: First TRUE condition wins; TRUE literal acts as catch-all

IFS_no_match_no_catchall.description: No condition true and no catch-all -> #N/A

IFS_order_matters.description: Conditions evaluated left-to-right; first match short-circuits
IFS_order_matters.notes: A1>10 is also true but never reached

IFS_catchall_first_value.description: TRUE as the first condition always wins regardless of position

INDEX_whole_column_spill.description: row_num=0 returns the entire column as a spilled array

INDEX_MATCH_combo.description: Classic INDEX/MATCH pattern used as a VLOOKUP replacement

INDIRECT_basic_cell_text.description: Basic ref_text naming a cell literally

INDIRECT_concatenated_ref.description: ref_text built dynamically by concatenating column letter and a row number

INDIRECT_malformed_ref_error.description: A ref_text string that isn't a valid cell reference in either A1 or R1C1 style -> #REF!
INDIRECT_malformed_ref_error.notes: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/indirect-function-474b3a3a-8a26-4f44-b491-92b6306fa261 -- documents that an invalid ref_text returns the #REF! error value

INDIRECT_r1c1_style.description: a1=FALSE switches ref_text parsing to R1C1 notation; R2C1 means row 2, column 1 = A2

INDIRECT_ref_to_blank_cell.description: Referencing a genuinely blank cell returns 0, matching normal cell-reference behavior in a numeric context

INDIRECT_missing_sheet_ref_error.description: ref_text names a sheet that does not exist in the workbook -> #REF!, the unguarded baseline for the IFERROR/ISERROR/ISREF guard cases in the sibling test files
INDIRECT_missing_sheet_ref_error.notes: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/indirect-function-474b3a3a-8a26-4f44-b491-92b6306fa261 -- documents that ref_text which is not a valid reference returns the #REF! error value

INT_basic_positive.description: Positive fractional number truncates its decimal part

INT_negative_rounds_toward_negative_infi.description: Documented classic divergence from TRUNC: INT always rounds DOWN to the nearest integer (toward negative infinity), so a negative fractional number rounds AWAY from zero
INT_negative_rounds_toward_negative_infi.notes: Per Microsoft's INT function docs, INT(-8.9) = -9 because INT rounds down toward negative infinity, unlike TRUNC(-8.9) = -8 which truncates toward zero -- see the paired TRUNC_negative_truncates_toward_zero case in TRUNC.json for the direct comparison

INT_already_integer.description: A whole number is returned unchanged

INT_negative_integer.description: A whole negative number is returned unchanged (no fractional part to drop)

INTERCEPT_exact_line.description: Points on y=2x+1 exactly: least-squares intercept must be exactly 1

IPMT_first_month_interest.description: First-month interest on the $300k/6% mortgage: exactly principal x monthly rate = 1500

IRR_simple_investment.description: -1000 followed by three 500s: the rate where NPV=0 is ~23.4% (mathematically determined root; all engines must converge to it)

ISBLANK_true_for_genuinely_empty_cell.description: A1 is never written to at all (no setup_cells entry) -- a genuinely empty cell

ISBLANK_false_for_formula_returning_empt.description: A1 contains the formula ="" which displays as nothing but is NOT considered blank -- a classic documented divergence between 'looks empty' and 'is blank'. Verified via https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/823838/the-result-is-false-when-you-use-the-isblank-function-in-an-excel-spre ("the result is FALSE even though the cell appears to be empty ... when the cell contains a zero-length string")
ISBLANK_false_for_formula_returning_empt.notes: A1 displays as blank but holds a zero-length-string formula result, not a true blank -- ISBLANK must return FALSE

ISBLANK_false_for_cell_with_value.description: A1 explicitly contains the value 0 -- clearly not blank

ISERR_div0.description: ISERR is TRUE for a #DIV/0! error (any error except #N/A)

ISERR_na.description: Key distinguishing case: ISERR is documented to return FALSE specifically for #N/A, unlike ISERROR (TRUE) -- 'ISERR: Value refers to any error value except #N/A' per https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665
ISERR_na.notes: This is the whole point of ISERR existing separately from ISERROR: it deliberately excludes #N/A.

ISERR_value_error.description: ISERR is TRUE for a #VALUE! error (not #N/A, so it counts)

ISERROR_div0.description: ISERROR is TRUE for a #DIV/0! error, one of ANY error type it catches (per support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665)

ISERROR_na.description: ISERROR is also TRUE for #N/A specifically (unlike ISERR, which excludes #N/A) -- contrast with ISERR_na and ISNA_na in the sibling test files

ISERROR_value_error.description: ISERROR is TRUE for a #VALUE! error (text coerced into arithmetic)

ISERROR_indirect_missing_sheet.description: ISERROR over an INDIRECT naming a sheet that does not exist: the #REF! is an error value, so TRUE
ISERROR_indirect_missing_sheet.notes: Microsoft documents ISERROR as TRUE for any error value (#N/A, #VALUE!, #REF!, #DIV/0!, #NUM!, #NAME? or #NULL!): https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665

ISEVEN_negative_odd.description: A negative odd number -> FALSE (docs' own example is =ISEVEN(-1) -> FALSE)

ISEVEN_noninteger_truncates.description: Non-integer input is truncated toward zero before testing, per Microsoft docs' own example: '=ISEVEN(2.5) ... The decimal portion is truncated, so 2 is tested.' -> TRUE

ISEVEN_zero.description: Zero is documented as even -> TRUE

ISFORMULA_true_on_formula_cell.description: A1 contains a live formula (=1+2), so ISFORMULA must return TRUE

ISFORMULA_false_on_literal.description: B1 holds a plain number, so FALSE

ISLOGICAL_true.description: TRUE is a logical value -> TRUE

ISLOGICAL_false.description: FALSE is a logical value -> TRUE

ISLOGICAL_number.description: A plain number is not a logical value -> FALSE
ISLOGICAL_number.notes: Even though 1 and TRUE are arithmetically interchangeable, ISLOGICAL distinguishes the underlying boolean type from a number.

ISLOGICAL_text.description: Text is not a logical value -> FALSE
ISLOGICAL_text.notes: The text string "TRUE" is text, not the boolean TRUE.

ISNA_div0.description: Key distinguishing case: ISNA is FALSE for #DIV/0! -- it only recognizes #N/A specifically, per https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665 ('ISNA: Value refers to the #N/A error value')

ISNA_na.description: ISNA is TRUE only for #N/A, the one case where ISERR disagrees with ISERROR/ISNA

ISNA_value_error.description: ISNA is FALSE for a #VALUE! error (not #N/A)

ISNUMBER_boolean.description: Documented divergence/point of confusion: a logical TRUE/FALSE value is its own distinct type in Excel's IS-function type system and is NOT considered a number, even though it participates in arithmetic as 1/0. Microsoft's IS-functions page (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665) states value arguments 'are not converted' and gives ISLOGICAL as the dedicated test for booleans, distinct from ISNUMBER -- the docs do not give an explicit ISNUMBER(TRUE) example, but this is the well-established, widely verified real Excel result.
ISNUMBER_boolean.notes: ISNUMBER(TRUE) = FALSE; use ISLOGICAL to detect booleans instead.; MISMATCH vs expected: expected False, got True

ISODD_noninteger_truncates.description: Non-integer input is truncated toward zero before testing (3.9 -> 3, odd) per https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/isodd-function-1208a56d-4f10-4f44-a5fc-648cafd6c07a ('If number is not an integer, it is truncated.')

ISODD_zero.description: Zero is even, so ISODD(0) -> FALSE

ISOWEEKNUM_doc_example.description: Microsoft's own documented example date/result. Verified via https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/isoweeknum-function-1c2d0afe-d25b-4ab1-8894-8d0520e90e0e

ISOWEEKNUM_prior_iso_year_boundary.description: Genuine algorithmic divergence from plain WEEKNUM: ISO 8601 week 1 is defined as the week containing the year's first Thursday (Monday-start weeks), NOT the week containing Jan 1. Jan 1, 2023 is a Sunday, so it belongs to the week Dec 26, 2022 - Jan 1, 2023, whose Thursday (Dec 29, 2022) is in 2022 -- so this date is ISO week 52 of 2022, even though plain WEEKNUM would call it week 1 of 2023
ISOWEEKNUM_prior_iso_year_boundary.notes: Cross-checked against Python's datetime.date(2023,1,1).isocalendar() -> (2022, 52, 7), which implements ISO 8601

ISOWEEKNUM_same_calendar_date_different_.description: Contrast case: Jan 1, 2024 is a Monday, so (unlike the 2023 case above) it DOES start ISO week 1 of 2024 -- showing the year-boundary quirk depends entirely on which weekday Jan 1 falls on

ISOWEEKNUM_next_iso_year_boundary.description: The same phenomenon at the OTHER end of the year: Dec 31, 2024 is a Tuesday, and the Monday-start week containing it (Dec 30, 2024 - Jan 5, 2025) has its Thursday (Jan 2, 2025) in the following calendar year, so this December date is actually ISO week 1 of 2025

ISREF_indirect_missing_sheet.description: INDIRECT could not resolve to a reference (no such sheet), so ISREF is FALSE -- the basis of the IF(ISREF(...)) guard pattern
ISREF_indirect_missing_sheet.notes: Microsoft documents ISREF as TRUE when value refers to a reference and FALSE otherwise; an unresolvable INDIRECT yields no reference: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665

ISREF_indirect_valid.description: INDIRECT resolves to a real cell reference on the current sheet, so ISREF is TRUE
ISREF_indirect_valid.notes: Microsoft documents ISREF as TRUE when value refers to a reference: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/is-functions-0f2d7971-6019-40a0-a171-f2d869135665

ISTEXT_boolean.description: A logical value is not text -> FALSE

LARGE_k1_equals_max.description: k=1 returns the same value as MAX

LARGE_k_out_of_range.description: k larger than the count of values -> #NUM!

LARGE_k_zero_error.description: k=0 is also out of the valid 1..n range -> #NUM!

LEFT_num_chars_exceeds_length.description: num_chars larger than the string length returns the whole string, not an error

LET_chained_bindings.description: Later bindings can reference earlier ones in the same LET

LINEST_slope_exact_line.description: Slope element of LINEST on exact y=2x+1 data must be exactly 2

LN_zero_error.notes: Microsoft's LN docs specify the Number argument must be 'the positive real number for which you want the natural logarithm' -- https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ln-function-81fe1ed7-dac9-4acd-ba1d-07a142c6118f -- 0 and negative numbers are outside that domain and both are well-established to raise #NUM!, matching every other Excel logarithm function; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#NUM!', got '#VALUE!'

LN_negative_error.description: Negative numbers are outside LN's domain -> #NUM!

LOG_default_base_ten.description: With base omitted, LOG defaults to base 10
LOG_default_base_ten.notes: Microsoft's LOG docs state 'If base is omitted, it is assumed to be 10' -- https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/log-function-4e82f196-1ca9-4747-8fb0-6c4a3abb3280

LOG_explicit_base.description: Explicit base argument: log base 2 of 8

LOG_negative_number_error.description: Negative numbers are outside LOG's domain -> #NUM!

LOG10_negative_error.description: Negative numbers are outside LOG10's domain -> #NUM!

LOOKUP_vector_exact_match.description: Vector form exact match against an ascending-sorted lookup_vector
LOOKUP_vector_exact_match.notes: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/lookup-function-446d94af-663b-451d-8251-369d5e3864cb -- lookup_vector must be in ascending order for LOOKUP to work correctly; this vector is sorted

LOOKUP_vector_approximate_between_values.description: No exact match; LOOKUP uses the largest lookup_vector value that is <= lookup_value
LOOKUP_vector_approximate_between_values.notes: 3.5 has no exact match; largest value <=3.5 is 3 -> paired result 30

LOOKUP_below_range_na.description: lookup_value smaller than every entry in lookup_vector -> #N/A

LOOKUP_array_form_more_rows_than_cols.description: Array form (single 2-D argument, no separate result_vector): since A1:B3 has more rows than columns, LOOKUP searches the FIRST column and returns from the LAST column
LOOKUP_array_form_more_rows_than_cols.notes: Per Microsoft docs' array-form rule (searches first row/col depending on which is longer): match on A2=2 returns paired last-column value 200

LOWER_leaves_numbers_and_symbols.description: Digits and symbols have no case and are left unchanged

MAKEARRAY_rc.description: Build a 2x2 array where each cell = row*col
MAKEARRAY_rc.notes: MISMATCH vs expected: value mismatch: expected 1, got '#NAME?'

MAP_double.description: Apply a lambda to each element (double it)
MAP_double.notes: MISMATCH vs expected: value mismatch: expected 2, got '#NAME?'

MATCH_approx_ascending.description: match_type 1 (default): largest value <= lookup, ascending sorted data
MATCH_approx_ascending.notes: Position 2 holds value 2, the largest value <= 3

MATCH_approx_descending.description: match_type -1: smallest value >= lookup, descending sorted data
MATCH_approx_descending.notes: Position 3 holds value 4, the smallest value >= 3 in descending data

MAX_basic.description: Largest value in a simple numeric range

MAX_negative_numbers.description: Largest of a set that includes negative numbers

MAX_ignores_text.description: Text values in the range are ignored, not treated as 0
MAX_ignores_text.notes: MAX skips non-numeric text cells entirely rather than erroring or treating them as 0

MAX_empty_range.description: A range with no numeric values at all returns 0
MAX_empty_range.notes: MAX of an empty/all-blank range is documented to return 0

MAXIFS_single_criteria.description: Max of A where paired B > 2

MAXIFS_no_matches.description: No rows satisfy the criteria -> 0 (not an error)

MEDIAN_odd_count.description: With an odd count of numbers, MEDIAN is the single middle value once sorted

MEDIAN_even_count_averages_middle_two.description: With an even count of numbers, MEDIAN averages the two middle values
MEDIAN_even_count_averages_middle_two.notes: Sorted: 1,2,3,4 -> middle two are 2 and 3 -> average 2.5

MEDIAN_ignores_text_and_blanks.description: Text values and blank cells in a range argument are ignored (not counted as 0 and not counted toward the element count)
MEDIAN_ignores_text_and_blanks.notes: Only 10, 20, 30 are numeric -> odd count of 3 -> middle value is 20; if blanks/text counted as 0 this would shift the median

MEDIAN_single_value.description: Degenerate single-value case returns that value

MID_basic.description: Basic extraction of 3 characters starting at position 2

MID_start_beyond_length.description: start_num beyond the string length returns an empty string, not an error
MID_start_beyond_length.notes: Microsoft docs: "If start_num is greater than the length of text, MID returns \"\" (empty text)." Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/mid-midb-functions-d5f9e25c-d7d6-472e-b568-4ecb12433028

MID_num_chars_exceeds_remaining.description: num_chars larger than the number of characters remaining returns just what's left, not an error or padded result

MID_start_num_one_full_length.description: start_num=1 with num_chars covering the whole string returns the whole string

MIN_basic.description: Smallest value in a simple numeric range

MIN_negative_numbers.description: Negative numbers are correctly ordered below positives

MIN_ignores_text.description: Text values in the range are ignored, not treated as 0
MIN_ignores_text.notes: MIN skips non-numeric text cells entirely rather than erroring or treating them as 0

MIN_empty_range.description: A range with no numeric values at all returns 0
MIN_empty_range.notes: MIN of an empty/all-blank range is documented to return 0

MINIFS_single_criteria.description: Min of A where paired B > 2

MINIFS_no_matches.description: No rows satisfy the criteria -> 0 (not an error)

MINUTE_of_fractional_day_noon.description: MINUTE applied to a bare fractional-day serial -- exactly noon has 0 minutes past the hour

MINUTE_of_time_value.description: MINUTE applied to a TIME()-constructed value

MINUTE_of_time_near_midnight.description: MINUTE just before a day boundary

MOD_negative_dividend.description: Excel/LO MOD result takes the SIGN OF THE DIVISOR, not truncated-remainder semantics
MOD_negative_dividend.notes: C-style '%' would give -1; spreadsheet MOD gives 2 because result = n - d*FLOOR(n/d)

MOD_negative_divisor.description: Negative divisor: result takes the sign of the divisor

MODE_MULT_two_modes.description: Returns every value tied for most frequent as a spilled vertical array; 1 and 2 each appear twice

MODE_MULT_single_mode.description: With one clear most-frequent value, returns just that value

MODE_SNGL_basic.description: Returns the single most frequently occurring value

MODE_SNGL_from_range.description: Most frequent value read from a cell range

MODE_SNGL_first_of_ties.description: When two values tie for most frequent, returns the one that appears first

MODE_SNGL_no_repeats_error.description: Errors when no value repeats. Excel and Google Sheets return #N/A here; LibreOffice Calc returns #VALUE! instead.

MODE_basic_repeated_value.description: Basic case with one clearly most-frequent value
MODE_basic_repeated_value.notes: This is Microsoft's own documented MODE example data set -- https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/mode-function-e45192ce-9122-4980-82ed-4bdc34973120 -- 4 appears 3 times, more than any other value

MODE_no_repeated_value_na.description: When every value in the data set is unique (no duplicates at all), MODE has nothing to return
MODE_no_repeated_value_na.notes: Microsoft's MODE docs state verbatim: 'If the data set contains no duplicate data points, MODE returns the #N/A error value' -- https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/mode-function-e45192ce-9122-4980-82ed-4bdc34973120; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#N/A', got '#VALUE!'

MODE_negative_numbers_repeated.description: MODE works the same way on negative numbers

MODE_ignores_text_and_blanks.description: Text values and blank cells in the range are ignored when finding the mode
MODE_ignores_text_and_blanks.notes: Only the numeric cells 1,1,2,3 participate; 1 is the most frequent among them

MONTH_of_date.description: MONTH applied to a constructed date

MONTH_of_raw_serial_epoch.description: MONTH applied directly to the raw serial number 1 (Jan 1, 1900)
MONTH_of_raw_serial_epoch.notes: Serial 1 is Jan 1, 1900 in the 1900 date system; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 1, got 12

MONTH_ignores_time_fraction.description: A serial with a fractional (time-of-day) component still resolves to the correct calendar month
MONTH_ignores_time_fraction.notes: 45366 = 2024-03-15; the .75 fractional day is ignored by MONTH

MROUND_basic.description: Rounds 10 to the nearest multiple of 3. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/mround-function-c299c3b0-15a5-426d-aa4b-d2d5b3baf427 (worked example)

MROUND_both_negative.description: Both arguments negative (same sign, as required) -> rounds to nearest multiple, sign preserved. Source: Microsoft MROUND docs worked example.

MROUND_fractional_multiple.description: Rounds 1.3 to the nearest multiple of the fractional value 0.2. Source: Microsoft MROUND docs worked example.
MROUND_fractional_multiple.notes: Microsoft's documented example rounds this to 1.4; true IEEE-754 double nearest value is 1.4000000000000001 (0.2*7), same well-known binary-float representation issue as ROUND(1.005,2) elsewhere in this corpus.

MROUND_mismatched_signs_error.description: Number and multiple must have the same sign, per Microsoft docs: 'The Number and Multiple arguments must have the same sign. If not, a #NUM error is returned.'

MROUND_zero.description: Zero rounds to zero regardless of the multiple.

MULTINOMIAL_two_groups.description: Ratio of the factorial of the sum to the product of factorials: 5!/(2!3!) = 10

N_number.description: A number passed through unchanged -> the number itself

N_true.description: TRUE -> 1, per Microsoft's N doc example table

N_false.description: FALSE -> 0, per the same doc's TRUE/FALSE convention

N_text.description: Text (even numeric-looking text like "7") -> 0, per doc example N("7") = 0 and N("Even") = 0: 'anything else' converts to 0

N_date.description: A date -> its underlying serial number, per doc example N(4/17/2011)=40650
N_date.notes: 2024-01-01 is Excel serial day 45292 under the 1900 date system.

NA_direct.description: NA() returns the #N/A error value itself

NA_isna_true.description: ISNA(NA()) must be TRUE -- confirms NA() genuinely produces the #N/A error

NA_propagates_through_arithmetic.description: The #N/A error propagates through arithmetic like any other error value

NA_isnumber_false.description: #N/A is an error, not a number -> FALSE

NETWORKDAYS_INTL_july.description: Working days in July 2026 with default weekend

NETWORKDAYS_basic_week.description: Mon Jan 1 to Fri Jan 5, 2024, no holidays -> 5 workdays

NETWORKDAYS_with_holiday.description: Same range excluding one holiday (Wed Jan 3) -> 4

NETWORKDAYS_reversed_dates.description: start_date after end_date returns a NEGATIVE count (not an error)

NETWORKDAYS_weekend_only.description: Sat Jan 6 to Sun Jan 7, 2024 -> 0 workdays

NOMINAL_inverse_of_effect.description: Inverting EFFECT recovers the 6% nominal rate

NOT_zero_coercion.description: 0 coerces to FALSE, so NOT(0) -> TRUE (same numeric-coercion convention as AND/OR/XOR)
NOT_zero_coercion.notes: Numeric coercion for logical functions confirmed via https://www.ablebits.com/office-addins-blog/excel-and-or-xor-not-functions/

NOT_nonzero_coercion.description: Any nonzero number coerces to TRUE, so NOT(5) -> FALSE

NOT_text_error.description: An arbitrary text literal cannot be coerced to a logical value -> #VALUE!

NOW_exists_and_plausible.description: Existence probe only: NOW() is volatile (changes every recalculation), so there is no fixed expected value
NOW_exists_and_plausible.notes: Non-deterministic by design; only check the engine recognizes the function and returns a plausible date-time serial

NOW_self_difference_is_deterministic.description: Two NOW() calls inside one cell evaluate in the same recalculation pass, so their difference is exactly 0 — a deterministic assertion about a volatile function (N() keeps the result a plain number instead of a duration-formatted cell)

NOW_on_or_after_today.description: NOW() includes today's date plus a time fraction, so it is always >= TODAY() within one recalculation

NPER_payoff_periods.description: Years to pay off 5000 at 10% with 1000/period: -ln(1-r*PV/pmt)/ln(1+r) = 7.2725

NPV_three_cashflows.description: 100/1.1 + 200/1.1^2 + 300/1.1^3 = 481.59 (NPV discounts the FIRST argument one period)

NUMBERVALUE_basic.description: Basic numeric text conversion with explicit US-style decimal_separator and group_separator arguments

NUMBERVALUE_european_separators.description: European-style formatted number: ',' is passed as decimal_separator and '.' as group_separator, letting NUMBERVALUE parse locale-formatted text regardless of the engine's own locale settings
NUMBERVALUE_european_separators.notes: Matches Microsoft's own documented example. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/numbervalue-function-1b05c8cf-2bfa-4437-af70-596c7ea7d879

NUMBERVALUE_malformed_text.description: Text that cannot be parsed as a number at all -> #VALUE!
NUMBERVALUE_malformed_text.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/numbervalue-function-1b05c8cf-2bfa-4437-af70-596c7ea7d879 - 'If any of the arguments are not valid, NUMBERVALUE returns the #VALUE! error value'

NUMBERVALUE_decimal_separator_used_twice.description: A decimal separator appearing more than once in the text is documented as invalid input -> #VALUE!
NUMBERVALUE_decimal_separator_used_twice.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/numbervalue-function-1b05c8cf-2bfa-4437-af70-596c7ea7d879 - decimal separator used multiple times is explicitly called out as an error condition

OCT2BIN_padded.description: The optional places argument pads the binary result to a fixed width

OCT2DEC_roundtrip.description: OCT2DEC reverses DEC2OCT, recovering the original number

ODD_round_up.description: Rounds up to the nearest odd integer

OFFSET_basic_single_cell.description: Move 2 rows down and 1 column right from A1, landing on B3

OFFSET_range_with_height_width.description: height=3, width=1 builds a 3-row-tall range starting 1 row below A1 (A2:A4), then sums it

OFFSET_negative_out_of_bounds_error.description: Offsetting above row 1 (off the top edge of the worksheet) -> #REF!
OFFSET_negative_out_of_bounds_error.notes: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/offset-function-c8de19ae-dd79-4b9b-a14e-b4d906d11b66 -- 'If rows and cols offset reference over the edge of the worksheet, OFFSET returns the #REF! error value.'; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#REF!', got '#VALUE!'

OFFSET_zero_offset_returns_same_cell.description: rows=0, cols=0 returns a reference to the exact starting cell

OR_range_numeric_with_nonzero.description: A range of numbers is coerced to logical (0=FALSE, nonzero=TRUE); one nonzero value makes the whole OR TRUE

OR_range_numeric_all_zero.description: A range of all-zero numbers coerces to all-FALSE -> FALSE

OR_range_text_ignored.description: Text within a range argument is ignored (not coerced, not an error), per https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/or-function-7d17ad14-8700-4281-b308-00b131e22af0: 'If an array or reference argument contains text or empty cells, those values are ignored.'

PEARSON_perfect_positive.description: Perfectly linear, same-direction data gives a correlation of 1

PEARSON_perfect_negative.description: Perfectly linear, opposite-direction data gives a correlation of -1

PEARSON_no_correlation.description: A symmetric pattern with no linear trend gives a correlation of 0. PEARSON returns the identical coefficient as CORREL.

PERCENTILE.EXC_k_zero_error.description: Documented divergence from PERCENTILE.INC: PERCENTILE.EXC requires k strictly between 0 and 1 (and more precisely between 1/(n+1) and n/(n+1)); k=0 -> #NUM!. Confirmed via Microsoft's PERCENTILE.EXC docs (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/percentile-exc-function-bbaa7204-e9e1-4010-85bf-c31dc5dce4ba): "If k is <=0 or if k >=1, PERCENTILE.EXC returns the #NUM! error value." PERCENTILE.INC_k_zero on identical data returns 1, not an error.

PERCENTILE.EXC_k_one_error.description: k=1 is likewise out of PERCENTILE.EXC's exclusive valid range -> #NUM!, whereas PERCENTILE.INC_k_one on identical data returns 10

PERCENTILE.EXC_k_half.description: k=0.5 is within the valid range for n=10 (1/11 < 0.5 < 10/11) and matches PERCENTILE.INC's result at the median

PERCENTILE.EXC_k_near_lower_bound.notes: pos=k*(n+1)=0.1*11=1.1 -> interpolate 10% of the way from data[0]=1 to data[1]=2 -> 1.1

PERCENTILE.INC_k_zero.description: k=0 is a valid boundary for PERCENTILE.INC and returns the minimum

PERCENTILE.INC_k_one.description: k=1 is a valid boundary for PERCENTILE.INC and returns the maximum

PERCENTILE.INC_k_half.description: k=0.5 (median); compare to PERCENTILE.EXC_k_half on identical data

PERCENTILE_median_equivalent.description: 50th percentile of 1,2,3,4 by linear interpolation = 2.5 (matches MEDIAN)

PERCENTRANK_middle.description: Rank of a value that sits at the third of four points (2/3 of the way up)

PERCENTRANK_interpolated.description: A value between two data points is interpolated (25 sits halfway between the 20 and 30 ranks)

PI_value.description: PI() takes no arguments and returns the double-precision approximation of pi

PI_rounded_four_places.description: Common real-world usage: rounding PI() to a fixed number of decimals

PI_times_two.description: PI() used directly in arithmetic (e.g. computing a full turn in radians)

PIVOTBY_exists_sum.description: Existence probe: pivot rows a/b vs columns x/y summing 1..4. In Excel 365 this spills a small pivot table (row+column headers and totals by default); exact layout depends on optional args, so we only assert the engine recognizes the function (not #NAME?)
PIVOTBY_exists_sum.notes: Probe only: spilled pivot layout (headers/totals) varies with optional args; the key datum is whether the engine has PIVOTBY at all

PMT_standard_mortgage.description: Monthly payment on a $300k 30-year loan at 6% annual: the standard amortization formula gives $1,798.65

POWER_negative_exponent.description: Negative exponent gives a reciprocal power

POWER_fractional_exponent_positive_base.description: Fractional exponent on a positive base is a well-defined real root (square root here)

POWER_negative_base_fractional_exponent.description: A negative base raised to a non-integer exponent has no real-number result in general (would require complex numbers), so Excel errors
POWER_negative_base_fractional_exponent.notes: Confirmed via Microsoft's own community support: entering =(-8)^(2/3) (equivalent power semantics to POWER) returns #NUM! in Excel -- https://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/msoffice/forum/all/excel-calculating-exponential-of-negative-number/5c67eae2-5682-4daf-b3d6-50b22e9919c2 -- note that -8^(1/3) is mathematically -2 as a real cube root, but Excel's POWER/^ implementation does not special-case rational exponents with odd integer denominators and returns #NUM! for any negative base with a non-integer exponent; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#NUM!', got -2

POWER_zero_to_zero.description: 0 raised to the 0th power; by the near-universal 'empty product' convention this is 1 (matches VBA's own '0^0', Python, C#, and LibreOffice/OpenOffice Calc)
POWER_zero_to_zero.notes: Real Excel (the worksheet function, and even the '^' operator) has a long-standing, Microsoft-acknowledged bug -- reproduced in Excel 2007 and 2010 and still reported unresolved -- where both '=0^0' and '=POWER(0,0)' incorrectly return #NUM! instead of 1, even though VBA's own 'x = 0 ^ 0' correctly evaluates to 1 in the same product. Recording the spec/cross-engine-consensus value (1) as 'expected' here so this exact Excel quirk shows up as a flagged divergence rather than being silently baked in as 'correct' -- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4850441/excel-formula-bug-00-gives-num

PPMT_first_month_principal.description: First-month principal: total payment 1798.65 minus 1500 interest

PROPER_basic_sentence.description: Basic multi-word capitalization: the first letter of each word is capitalized, the rest lowercased

PROPER_digit_letter_boundary.description: Microsoft's own documented example: PROPER treats any non-letter (including a run of digits) as a word boundary, so the letter immediately following the digits is also capitalized and treated as a new word-start

PROPER_apostrophe_word_boundary.description: PROPER treats an apostrophe as a word boundary too, capitalizing the letter that follows it -- so a name like o'brien becomes O'Brien. Widely reproduced/documented real PROPER behavior (the same non-letter-is-a-boundary rule Microsoft documents for the digit case above), though this exact example isn't on Microsoft's own reference page

PV_annuity.description: Present value of $1,000/year for 5 years at 10%: 1000*(1-1.1^-5)/0.1

QUARTILE_EXC_median.description: The second quartile is the median; for 1..5 that is 3

QUARTILE_EXC_first.description: The exclusive first quartile interpolates at rank 0.25*(n+1); for 1..5 that is 1.5

QUARTILE_EXC_third.description: The exclusive third quartile for 1..5 is 4.5

QUARTILE.INC_quart_two_median.description: quart=2 returns the median, equal to PERCENTILE.INC(...,0.5)

QUARTILE.INC_quart_out_of_range.description: quart must be an integer 0-4; 5 is out of range -> #NUM!

QUARTILE_first_quartile.description: Q1 of 1,2,3,4 under the inclusive linear-interpolation method Excel uses = 1.75

QUOTIENT_integer_division.description: Integer part of 17/5, discarding the remainder

RADIANS_negative.description: Negative degrees convert to negative radians

RAND_exists_and_in_unit_range.description: Existence probe only: RAND() is non-deterministic; we just confirm the engine recognizes the function (not #NAME?) and returns a plausible value
RAND_exists_and_in_unit_range.notes: Non-deterministic by design; harness should only check 0<=value<1 and absence of #NAME?

RANDARRAY_shape_is_deterministic.description: Values are random but the requested shape is not: a 2x3 RANDARRAY must have 2 rows and 3 columns (encoded as 23)

RANDARRAY_default_unit_range.description: With no min/max arguments, every value is a decimal in [0,1) — deterministic bounds on non-deterministic values

RANDBETWEEN_exists_bounds.description: Existence probe: confirm recognized and result plausible (integer 1..10)
RANDBETWEEN_exists_bounds.notes: Non-deterministic by design; harness should only check 1<=value<=10 and absence of #NAME?

RANDBETWEEN_degenerate_equal_bounds.description: When bottom==top the result is deterministic

RANDBETWEEN_negative_range.description: Existence probe with an all-negative range

RANK.AVG_tie_averages_ranks.description: Documented divergence from RANK.EQ: tied values get the AVERAGE of the ranks they would occupy, not the top rank. Per Microsoft's RANK.AVG docs (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/rank-avg-function-bd406a6f-eb38-4d73-aa8e-6d1c3c72e83a): "If more than one value has the same rank, the average rank is returned."
RANK.AVG_tie_averages_ranks.notes: The two tied 20s would occupy ranks 3 and 4 (descending); average = (3+4)/2 = 3.5, vs RANK.EQ's 3 on identical data

RANK.AVG_no_tie_matches_RANK_EQ.description: With no ties, RANK.AVG matches RANK.EQ exactly

RANK.AVG_tie_ascending_order.description: Tie-averaging also applies with the ascending order argument
RANK.AVG_tie_ascending_order.notes: Ascending, the two tied 20s would occupy ranks 2 and 3 (only 10 is smaller); average = 2.5

RANK.EQ_basic_descending.description: RANK.EQ is the modern equivalent of RANK; identical data/formula to RANK_basic_descending must give the identical result

RANK.EQ_ascending_order.description: Nonzero order argument ranks ascending (smallest=1), matching RANK's behavior

RANK.EQ_tie_shares_top_rank.description: Like legacy RANK, ties get the same top rank (contrast with RANK.AVG's averaged rank on identical data, see RANK.AVG_tie_averages_ranks)

RANK_basic_descending.notes: Only 40 is greater than 30, so 30 is rank 2

RANK_ascending_order.notes: 10,20,20 are all less than 30, so 30 is rank 4 ascending

RANK_tie_shares_top_rank.description: Tied values share the same (best/top) rank
RANK_tie_shares_top_rank.notes: Two values (30,40) exceed 20, so both 20s tie for rank 3; rank 4 is skipped entirely

RATE_recover_annual_rate.description: Inverting the PMT mortgage case: 360 payments of $1,798.65 on $300k recovers the 6% annual rate (iterative solver; all engines must converge)

REDUCE_sum.description: Accumulate a range into a single value (sum)

REPLACE_basic_by_position.description: Replaces the first 3 characters by position, regardless of what they are

REPLACE_position_vs_content_contrast.description: REPLACE targets characters purely by position (start_num/num_chars), unlike SUBSTITUTE which matches by content: here characters 2-4 ('ana') are removed and replaced with 'XYZ' regardless of what they spell
REPLACE_position_vs_content_contrast.notes: 'banana' = b(1)a(2)n(3)a(4)n(5)a(6); removing positions 2-4 ('ana') and inserting 'XYZ' gives 'b' + 'XYZ' + 'na' = 'bXYZna'

REPLACE_larger_range.description: Replaces a 5-character mid-string range (positions 6-10) with a single character

REPT_zero_times.description: number_times=0 returns an empty string, not an error
REPT_zero_times.notes: Microsoft docs: "If number_times is 0 (zero), REPT returns \"\" (empty text)." Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/rept-function-04c4d778-e712-43b4-9c15-d656582bb061

REPT_negative_times.notes: Documented behavior: REPT does not accept negative number_times and returns #VALUE! (per Microsoft's REPT reference and its documented remarks on the number_times argument)

REPT_fractional_truncated.description: A non-integer number_times is truncated toward zero before repeating
REPT_fractional_truncated.notes: Documented: "If number_times is not an integer, it is truncated."

RIGHT_basic.description: Basic extraction of the last 3 characters

RIGHT_num_chars_exceeds_length.description: num_chars larger than the string length returns the whole string, not an error

ROUND_half_away_from_zero.description: Excel/LO ROUND uses arithmetic rounding (half away from zero), NOT banker's rounding (round-half-to-even)
ROUND_half_away_from_zero.notes: Banker's rounding would give 2; correct spreadsheet behavior is 3

ROUND_negative_half_away_from_zero.description: Negative half-values also round away from zero

ROUND_negative_digits.description: Negative num_digits rounds to the left of the decimal point

ROUND_float_representation_quirk.description: Tests whether the engine falls into the naive-binary-float trap: the IEEE-754 double closest to 1.005 is actually ~1.00499999999999989, so a naive floor(x*100+0.5)/100 implementation would round DOWN to 1.00
ROUND_float_representation_quirk.notes: Both Excel and LibreOffice correctly return 1.01, not 1.0 -- they normalize to ~15 significant decimal digits before rounding, specifically to avoid this well-known binary-float pitfall

ROUNDDOWN_basic_positive.description: Always rounds toward zero, regardless of the discarded digit

ROUNDDOWN_negative_number.description: For negative numbers, 'down' means toward zero (less negative), not toward negative infinity

ROUNDDOWN_negative_num_digits.description: Negative num_digits rounds to the left of the decimal point (nearest multiple of 10 here)
ROUNDDOWN_negative_num_digits.notes: Rounding 21.5 down (toward zero) to the nearest 10 gives 20 -- this is Microsoft's own documented example for ROUNDDOWN, and the direct counterpart to ROUNDUP(21.5,-1)=30

ROUNDDOWN_decimal_places.description: Rounds down to 2 decimal places, discarding the remaining digits

ROUNDUP_basic_positive.description: Always rounds away from zero, regardless of the discarded digit

ROUNDUP_negative_number.description: For negative numbers, 'up' means away from zero (more negative), not toward positive infinity

ROUNDUP_negative_num_digits.description: Negative num_digits rounds to the left of the decimal point (nearest multiple of 10 here)
ROUNDUP_negative_num_digits.notes: Rounding 21.5 up (away from zero) to the nearest 10 gives 30 -- this is Microsoft's own documented example for ROUNDUP

ROUNDUP_decimal_places.description: Rounds up to 2 decimal places even though the 3rd decimal (1) would round down normally

ROW_no_arg_uses_formula_cell.description: No argument: ROW() returns the row of the cell containing the formula itself. This case's formula lands in cell F1 by default, which is row 1
ROW_no_arg_uses_formula_cell.notes: The harness writes each case's formula into cell F1 (row 1, column 6); ROW() with no anchor argument returns the formula's own row, i.e. 1

ROW_explicit_cell_ref.description: Explicit single-cell reference argument overrides the formula's own location

ROW_range_returns_first_row.description: In non-array (scalar) context, ROW() of a multi-row range returns the row number of the FIRST row of the reference

ROW_far_cell.description: Sanity check with a larger row number

ROWS_basic_column_range.description: Height (row count) of a single-column range; does not depend on cell contents

ROWS_single_cell.description: A single cell reference has exactly 1 row

ROWS_2d_range.description: Row count of a 2-D range only counts rows, ignoring the 3 columns

RSQ_perfect_fit.description: A perfectly linear relationship has an R-squared of 1 (all variance explained)

RSQ_no_fit.description: Data with no linear relationship has an R-squared of 0. RSQ equals CORREL squared.

SCAN_running_sum.notes: MISMATCH vs expected: value mismatch: expected 1, got '#NAME?'

SEARCH_case_insensitive_match.description: SEARCH is case-insensitive: lowercase 'a' matches the leading uppercase 'A' -> position 1 (contrast with FIND on this exact same input, which is case-sensitive and returns #VALUE!)

SEARCH_wildcard_asterisk.description: SEARCH supports wildcards unlike FIND: '*' matches any sequence of characters, so "p*e" matches the substring "pple" starting at position 2
SEARCH_wildcard_asterisk.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/search-function-9ab04538-0e55-4719-a72e-b6f54513b495 - SEARCH allows the wildcard characters '?' and '*' in find_text; FIND does not support wildcards at all

SEARCH_wildcard_question_mark.description: '?' wildcard matches exactly one character, so "?pple" matches "Apple" starting at position 1

SEARCH_not_found.description: find_text not present anywhere in within_text -> #VALUE!

SECOND_of_fractional_day_noon.description: SECOND applied to a bare fractional-day serial -- exactly noon has 0 seconds past the minute

SECOND_of_time_value.description: SECOND applied to a TIME()-constructed value

SECOND_of_time_near_midnight.description: SECOND just before a day boundary

SEQUENCE_basic_vertical.description: Default rows-only sequence starting at 1, step 1

SEQUENCE_rows_cols.description: 2 rows x 3 columns filled row-major from 1

SHEET_returns_positive_index.description: SHEET() returns the current sheet's 1-based index; the absolute number depends on workbook structure (our harness batches many test sheets into one workbook), so we assert the invariant instead

SHEETS_returns_positive_count.description: SHEETS() counts sheets in the workbook; the harness workbook holds one sheet per test case, so we assert the invariant rather than a fixed count

SIGN_zero.description: Zero returns 0, not an error -- SIGN never errors on a numeric input

SIGN_small_negative_fraction.description: Any negative value, no matter how small, still returns -1

SLOPE_exact_line.description: Points on y=2x+1 exactly: least-squares slope must be exactly 2

SMALL_k1_equals_min.description: k=1 returns the same value as MIN

SMALL_k_out_of_range.description: k larger than the count of values -> #NUM!
SMALL_k_out_of_range.notes: Only 5 values exist; requesting the 6th-smallest is out of range; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#NUM!', got '#VALUE!'

SMALL_k_zero_error.description: k=0 is also out of the valid 1..n range -> #NUM!

SORT_by_second_column.description: 2D range sorted by its second column ascending

SORT_empty_range_error.description: Sorting a single blank cell (degenerate case)
SORT_empty_range_error.notes: Blank cell sorts as 0 in numeric context; no error expected; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 0, got '#VALUE!'

SORTBY_by_other_col.description: Sort column A by the values in column B (ascending)

SQRT_zero.description: Square root of zero is zero

SQRT_negative_returns_num_error.description: Negative input has no real square root -> #NUM!
SQRT_negative_returns_num_error.notes: Microsoft's SQRT docs state verbatim: 'If number is negative, SQRT returns the #NUM! error value' -- https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Excel/functions/sqrt-function; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#NUM!', got '#VALUE!'

SQRT_documented_abs_workaround.description: Microsoft's own SQRT documentation demonstrates wrapping a possibly-negative argument in ABS as the standard workaround to avoid #NUM!
SQRT_documented_abs_workaround.notes: Same doc page above shows an example using '=SQRT(ABS(A2))' specifically to sidestep the negative-input #NUM! case

STANDARDIZE_above_mean.description: Converts a value to a z-score: 50 is two standard deviations above a mean of 40

STANDARDIZE_at_mean.description: A value equal to the mean has a z-score of 0

STANDARDIZE_below_mean.description: A value below the mean gives a negative z-score

STDEV.P_diverges_from_sample_same_data.description: Population standard deviation on the SAME dataset {2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9} used for STDEV/STDEV.S - divides by n instead of n-1, giving a smaller, exact result (2) vs the sample stdev's 2.138089935299395

STDEV.P_two_points_diverges.description: Same two-point data as the sample-stdev cases (10,20) but population formula divides by n=2 instead of n-1=1, giving a much smaller result
STDEV.P_two_points_diverges.notes: Population variance=((10-15)^2+(20-15)^2)/2=25; sqrt(25)=5, vs sample stdev's 7.0710678118654755 on identical data

STDEV.P_single_value_no_error.description: Unlike STDEV.S/STDEV, a single value does NOT error for the population formula, since it divides by n (=1), not n-1
STDEV.P_single_value_no_error.notes: Population variance of one point = 0/1 = 0, a valid result - genuine divergence from STDEV.S's #DIV/0! on the same single-cell input

STDEV.S_basic_two_points.description: Sample standard deviation of two hand-verifiable values, identical formula/data to STDEV_basic_two_points in the STDEV file

STDEV.S_matches_STDEV_same_data.description: STDEV.S on the classic Wikipedia sample dataset {2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9} - must match STDEV_matches_STDEV_S_same_data exactly, since STDEV.S is simply the Excel-2010+ modern name for the legacy STDEV calculation (same n-1 sample formula)

STDEV.S_single_value_div0.description: Sample stdev needs n>=2 (divides by n-1); one value -> #DIV/0!, confirmed against Microsoft's STDEV.S documentation of the n-1 method (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/stdev-s-function-7d69cf97-0c1f-4acf-be27-f3e83904cc23)

STDEV_basic_two_points.description: Sample standard deviation of two hand-verifiable values

STDEV_matches_STDEV_S_same_data.description: Legacy STDEV on the classic Wikipedia sample dataset {2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9}; compare to STDEV.S_matches_STDEV_same_data on identical data in the STDEV.S file - both must return exactly the same value since STDEV.S is just the modern name for the same sample-stdev calculation

STDEV_single_value_div0.description: Sample stdev needs at least 2 data points (divides by n-1); a single value -> #DIV/0!
STDEV_single_value_div0.notes: n-1=0 with a single supplied value, causing division by zero

STDEVA_numbers_only.description: For pure numbers STDEVA equals STDEV (sample standard deviation)

STDEVA_counts_text_as_zero.description: Unlike STDEV, STDEVA counts text as 0, so {2,4,"x"} is treated as {2,4,0}: sample standard deviation 2

STDEVA_identical_values.description: Identical values have zero standard deviation

STDEVP_textbook.description: Population standard deviation of the classic 8-value example (mean 5, variance 4)

STDEVP_two_values.description: Two values equidistant from their mean of 3 give a population standard deviation of 1

STDEVP_ignores_text.description: Text and blank cells are ignored, not treated as zero

STDEVPA_textbook.description: For pure numbers STDEVPA equals STDEVP (population standard deviation): the classic example gives 2

STDEVPA_counts_text_as_zero.description: Unlike STDEVP, STDEVPA counts text as 0, so {5,5,5,5,"x"} is treated as {5,5,5,5,0}: population standard deviation 2

SUBSTITUTE_all_occurrences.description: Without instance_num, every occurrence of old_text is replaced

SUBSTITUTE_instance_num.description: instance_num=2 replaces only the 2nd occurrence of old_text, leaving the 1st untouched

SUBSTITUTE_no_match.description: old_text not present in text returns the text unchanged

SUBSTITUTE_case_sensitive.description: SUBSTITUTE matches old_text case-sensitively; lowercase 'a' does not match the uppercase 'A' in "Apple", so the text is returned unchanged

SUBTOTAL_sum_code9.description: Function code 9 = SUM over visible rows (none hidden here)

SUBTOTAL_ignores_nested_subtotal.description: A5 contains its own SUBTOTAL over A1:A4; the outer SUBTOTAL must skip it (no double-count), so the answer is 100, not 200

SUM_basic_range.description: Basic sum of a contiguous numeric range

SUM_text_in_cell_reference_ignored.description: A text value stored in a referenced cell is IGNORED by SUM, not coerced to a number, even though it looks numeric
